scenes.text: Every household pays for subscriptions nobody uses. So you just ask. Eight hundred and three dollars, found. And it never spends a dollar on its own.
Every action waits in the tray with the exact price. One tap applies it. One tap takes it back. And the reversal lands in the ledger too.
Groceries ride Subscribe and Save. Five household essentials, bundled. Thirty-five dollars off, four fewer boxes on the road. And nothing is ordered until you tap.
Now the part parents care about. The profile switches to Leo, age nine. He asks for Robux. Blocked. The front door? Blocked. Not by a prompt. By the architecture. Nothing moves without a grown-up.
Trust isn't a promise. It's a proof. Rebuild three AM: every sensor, every decision, on the record.
And when the house needs something nobody coded, Hearth writes the tool itself. It understands the need, passes the safety gate, and mounts live as tool fifty-five.
Hearth. The house that runs itself, with receipts. And it's live right now. Not an agent. A servant.
